v.why: Replacing a missing input edge with a 3x3 conv restores connectivity and gains more than upgrading any existing op.
Filling an empty edge into the output with a strong conv gives a larger gain than replacing a weaker non-empty op.
An absent edge is the weakest parent, so adding a conv there has the most headroom.
Going from no edge to a 3x3 conv adds a whole path, a larger gain than swapping one op for another.
Adding the 1->2 conv where none existed adds capacity and gains more than replacing an existing op.
Upgrading from a 1x1 conv is a small step, so it gains less than upgrading from none or pooling.
Removing a 3x3 conv loses much more than removing a weak op, so the effect is more negative.
Removing a 3x3 conv on edge 4 is far more costly than removing a weak op.
Deleting a strong conv into the output hurts much more than deleting a weak op.
Replacing a useful skip on 0->3 gains less than replacing a none or pooling op, since the skip already helps.
